Yhdistelmäuuneja hankitaan yksi (1) kappale. Hankittavan laitteen tarkemmat ominaisuusvaatimukset sekä muut solmittavan hankintasopimuksen toteutuksen kannalta oleelliset seikat ovat ilmaistu tässä tarjouspyynnössä sekä sen liitteissä. title: Professional Services Supply Chain
description: The CRA has issued this Request for Proposal (RFP) to solicit bids from qualified professional services suppliers for contracts under the Professional Services Supply Chain (PSSC). The PSSC is the CRA’s suite of contracts for the provision of IT and certain non-IT professional services. Bidders must be able to supply consultants for every category and level after award. All responsive bids will be ranked, and contracts will be awarded to the five top-ranked bidders. Any requirements for consultants will then be competed amongst each of the contractors holding a contract. Bidders awarded a contract under the PSSC must provide consultants on an as-and-when requested basis, mainly for the CRA’s Information Technology Branch (ITB) within the National Capital Region (NCR); however, other branches and locations within the CRA may also make use of the PSSC. The work will be either remote or in-person. The period of the Contract is from April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2029 inclusive with options to extend the term of the contract by up to three additional one-year periods under the same conditions. The table below summarizes the total invoiced amounts under the Professional Services Supply Chain for the past three calendar years. January 1 – December 31 2023 - $61,283,633.32 January 1 – December 21 2024 - $41,421,783.98 January 1 – December 31 2025 - $15,606,254.92 As part of the Government of Canada’s (GC) continued commitment to responsible fiscal management, Budget 2023 announced significant reductions in discretionary spending on consulting, other professional services, and travel. The GC implemented $500 million in reductions in 2023-24, with ongoing annual reductions of $1.7 billion starting in 2024-25. Consequently, the CRA anticipates a continued decline in professional services procurement as it continues to realign resources to higher-priority areas. As the refocusing of GC spending is an ongoing process, however, the CRA is unable to quantify the extent of these reductions at this time. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to bidders of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements will be applied to contracts awarded pursuant to this solicitation. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. title: Chemical Residue and Allergen Testing in and on Food Products for Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
description: AMENDMENT TO CLOSING TIME: Please disregard the Ariba Discovery posting response deadline closing time and Buyandsell posting closing time. All required supporting documentation and bid submission must be submitted by 2026-10-16 at 2 p.m. EST. All bids submitted after 2 p.m. EST will result in the bid being declared non-responsive. This solicitation is for the requirement of analytical and laboratory services for the testing of chemical contaminants and/or allergens in foods, food crops, and tissues of food animals for the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA). Multiple contracts will be established as a result of this solicitation. The requirement is divided into two distinct parts. Part A: Categorized by commodity/food group for a total of 7 food groups (Dairy, Eggs, Fish & Seafood, Fresh Fruit & Vegetables, Honey, Meat, and Processed Products). Part B: Categorized by testing programs for a total of 24 programs (including 3-MCPD, Arsenic, BPA, Alternaria, Benzopyrene, etc.). An Offeror may submit an offer for one or multiple food groups in Part A and/or for one or more testing programs in Part B. Contracts awarded to bidders for multiple food groups and/or programs will be consolidated into a single contract. The full Submission of Offers and annexes can only be accessed and downloaded when logged into your SAP Ariba account and your Government of Canada profile has been approved by SAP Ariba. For technical support with SAP Ariba, please contact the CanadaBuys Service Desk.

title: Light Forces Enhancement
description: W8476-206234/C Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC) is requesting Industry feedback regarding the Light Forces Enhancement (LFE) project for the Government of Canada (GC), the Department of National Defence (DND), and the Canadian Armed Forces (CAF). The Canadian Light Forces (LF) need new light tactical personnel and cargo carrying capabilities. These capabilities will move soldiers and equipment across complex terrain which currently can only be reached on foot. It will lighten CAF soldiers’ on-person combat burden by carrying additional equipment and supplies, and will cover a larger area of operation through increased speed, range, and duration. This powerful, lightweight solution is expected to operate in domestic and expeditionary deployments, up to and including high threat environments. title: ITQ for iCDPSC (W8703-270048)
description: Public Services and Procurement Canada, on behalf of the Department of National Defence, invites suppliers to respond to this Invitation to Qualify (ITQ), which will qualify suppliers to participate in future procurement processes regarding the Interim Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability (iCDPSC). The Department of National Defence has a requirement to establish the Initial Operational Capability of the Canadian Deep Precision Strike Capability. The requirement includes an initial quantity of land-based launch systems, system support services, conventional precision-guided munitions, mission-planning and command-and-control systems, communications, support equipment, training, documentation, maintenance and technical support. The interim capability must be deployable, survivable, interoperable with Canadian and allied forces, and capable of delivering precise effects at extended ranges in contested operational environments. This ITQ is open to Canadian Suppliers and suppliers of the Five Eyes Alliance and the NATO community.
